nodes.proof_state:
If $a\geq b > 1,$ what is the largest possible value of $\log_{a}(a/b) + \log_{b}(b/a)?$

$
\mathrm{(A)}\ -2      \qquad
\mathrm{(B)}\ 0     \qquad
\mathrm{(C)}\ 2      \qquad
\mathrm{(D)}\ 3      \qquad
\mathrm{(E)}\ 4
$ Show that it is \textbf{B}.

If $a\geq b > 1,$ what is the largest possible value of $\log_{a}(a/b) + \log_{b}(b/a)?$

$
\mathrm{(A)}\ -2      \qquad
\mathrm{(B)}\ 0     \qquad
\mathrm{(C)}\ 2      \qquad
\mathrm{(D)}\ 3      \qquad
\mathrm{(E)}\ 4
$ Show that it is \textbf{B}.
["Let \( t=\log_a b \). Then \( 0<t\le 1 \) and the expression equals \( 2-t-1/t \).","When \( a=b \) the expression equals \( 0 \); it remains to show the expression is always \(\le 0\)."]
